tasks.short: Watch the recording for artifacts, check electrode contact, mark artifacts on the recording, and fix poor electrode contact.

steps.what: Neurodiagnostic technologist watches the recording for artifacts and interferences
Neurodiagnostic technologist checks electrode contact by measuring impedance by hand
Neurodiagnostic technologist indicates artifacts on electroneurodiagnostic recordings with typed annotations
Neurodiagnostic technologist fixes poor electrode contact

tasks.design: The recording software ({OTHER}) monitors electrode impedance during the test and warns when a channel passes a set limit, so the technologist does not measure by hand. Artifacts are marked with standard labels (electrode, movement, muscle, mains) instead of typed words; the technologist still marks each one and notes unusual ones. Recognising artifacts and fixing electrodes stay with the technologist; no software classifies the EEG.
tasks.previous_blocker: Impedance was checked by hand and artifacts annotated by typing.
tasks.enabler_now: Recording software monitors impedance and offers standard annotation labels.
tasks.still_hard: Some artifacts look like brain activity.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a chewing artifact from a seizure pattern.

evidence.claim: EEG recording software can monitor electrode impedance and offer standard annotation labels.
Software with a medical purpose is a medical device.

assumptions: Boundary: from the recording running to contact fixed; interpretation is outside.
Input contract: software set with impedance limits; fallback is checking by hand.

Recognising artifacts and fixing electrodes keep their full time. s2 keeps 30 for reading the warnings and checking flagged channels; s3 keeps 90 because a label replaces typing a standard word, and marking each artifact stays.
research_questions: Do neurologists find artifact marks more consistent?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: impedance limits are set once per test type.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older amplifiers do not monitor impedance, so half of tests are still measured by hand and s2 keeps 70 (7.0); high: all systems monitor impedance (13.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor the patient and recording during tests or surgery, note events with times, report changes to the neurologist or surgeon, and write the monitoring summary.

steps.what: Neurodiagnostic technologist monitors patients during tests or surgeries using EEG and video equipment
Neurodiagnostic technologist notes events with times: on paper today, with event buttons time-locked to the recording after the change
Neurodiagnostic technologist reports changes to the neurologist or surgeon
Neurodiagnostic technologist writes the monitoring summary

tasks.design: Events (seizure, movement, medication, stimulation) are marked with event buttons in the recording software ({OTHER}), time-locked to the EEG and video, so times are not written on paper and matched later; the technologist still marks each event. The monitoring summary template lists the marked events with times, and the technologist adds observations. Monitoring the patient and reporting changes stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Events were noted on paper and summaries written from those notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Recording software marks events time-locked to EEG and video.
tasks.still_hard: During surgery the technologist's hands are often busy.
tasks.human_edge: Warning the surgeon the moment a signal drops.

reach.learn: Whether events are easy to find.

evidence.claim: Recording software can mark events time-locked to EEG and video and list them in reports.

assumptions: Boundary: from the test running to the summary written; the neurologist's report is outside.
Input contract: event buttons set per test type; fallback is paper.

Monitoring and reporting keep their full time. s2 keeps 70 because times come from the recording and the technologist still marks each event; s4 keeps 70 because the event list fills in and the technologist writes the observations.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: event buttons are set once per test type.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: in surgery events are often called out and noted later, so s2 keeps 90 and s4 keeps 85 (3.0); high: events marked with buttons as designed (7.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the referral and record, ask the patient about medication, sleep and seizures, type the answers into the test system, and choose the test settings.

steps.what: Neurodiagnostic technologist reads the referral and record across several screens
Patient fills the questionnaire on medication, sleep and seizures in the patient portal before the test
Neurodiagnostic technologist collects patients' medical information about medication, sleep and seizures
Neurodiagnostic technologist types the answers into the test system
Neurodiagnostic technologist chooses the settings to customize tests

tasks.design: A referral view in the record ({OTHER}) shows the question, medication list and earlier recordings together. Patients fill a short questionnaire on medication, sleep and seizures in the patient portal before the test, and the answers appear in the test system, so the technologist confirms and adds instead of asking from scratch and typing. Choosing test settings stays with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information was gathered from several screens, asked from scratch and typed in.
tasks.enabler_now: Portals take pre-test questionnaires that flow into test systems.
tasks.still_hard: Patients with seizures may not remember details.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from a parent what the child's events really look like.
tasks.altitude: The technologist confirms information instead of typing it.

evidence.claim: Patient portals can take pre-test questionnaires that flow into test systems.
Health data are special category data under GDPR article 9.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the test customized; the test itself is outside.
Input contract: questionnaire linked to the test system; fallback is asking and typing.

Patients fill the questionnaire before the test (s1q, customer time). Choosing settings keeps its full time; s1 keeps 70 because the referral view replaces moving across screens and reading stays; s2 keeps 70 for confirming answers with the patient and adding what is missing; s3 keeps 30 for completing the answers in the test system.
Choosing settings stays with the technologist.

incremental.description: No separate new work: checking answers with the patient is in s2, and the patient's time is in s1q.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients fill the questionnaire, so the technologist asks and types as today and s2 keeps 95, s3 keeps 85 (12.5); high: most patients fill it (33.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain the test and reassure the patient, answer preparation questions by phone before the test, and note in the record that the patient was informed.

steps.what: Neurodiagnostic technologist explains testing procedures and reassures patients
Neurodiagnostic technologist answers patients' questions about test preparation by phone
Neurodiagnostic technologist notes in the record that the patient was informed

tasks.design: Each test has an information page with a short video in the patient portal ({OTHER}), covering preparation such as sleep deprivation and hair washing, so fewer patients phone with questions. That the patient was informed is still recorded in the test record; a tick box instead of a sentence takes the same time. Explaining and reassuring at the test stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation questions came by phone and information was noted in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient portals host information pages and videos per test.
tasks.still_hard: Parents of young children still call.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a child before electrodes go on.

evidence.claim: Patient portals can host information pages and videos linked to appointments.
Providers must inform patients about care and record it in the dossier.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient arrived to information recorded; the test is outside.
Input contract: information page per test; fallback is phone questions.
Patients read or watch the page before the test; a little patient time is priced.
Explaining at the test and recording that the patient was informed keep their full time. s2 keeps 60 because fewer patients phone.
research_questions: Do tests repeated for poor preparation fall?

incremental.description: Neurodiagnostic technologist keeps the information pages current.
Patients read the information page before the test.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients open the page, so calls hardly fall and s2 keeps 90 (0.5); high: fewer patients phone as designed (3.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The neurodiagnostic technologist keeps watching recordings, recognising artifacts, monitoring patients and reassuring them; hand impedance checks, paper event notes, typed history and phone questions shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using event marking and portal questionnaires
role.ambitious_version: A technologist with more time with patients.
